name: mskuibida-tooling
description: Maksym Skuibida's personal Claude Code tooling — small, opinionated plugins.

plugins.name: response-format
plugins.description: A house style for Claude's replies: one self-contained, fully linked, ask-first report at hand-back or when you are needed, quiet mid-flight, decisions through the question UI, and a hard bias against unverified claims.

plugins.name: worktree-cleanup
plugins.description: Find and remove orphaned git worktrees across many repos, gated on unpushed work, live sessions, and recent activity — re-verified at the moment of deletion, not at scan time.

plugins.name: model-fit
plugins.description: Before the first real task of a session, a quick Haiku check asks whether the session model fits it, on four tiers (Haiku, Sonnet, Opus, Fable); on a mismatch you get a Switch or Stay dialog before anything runs. It respects your cap and availableModels setting and, in auto, probes each model once a day; a transient error counts as available.

plugins.name: project-panel
plugins.description: A side pane for any repo with a plan: its sections, their items and what blocks the next one, with progress rings. Providers: AI-DLC v2, and a task ledger (WORKPLAN.md) read against its pull or merge requests (GitHub through gh, GitLab through glab, self-hosted included), with each pull request's review state and what it asks of you. Opens with /panel.

plugins.name: ask-guard
plugins.description: Keeps the question dialog readable: a question the model writes longer than 250 characters (configurable) is sent back with word to put the context in a markdown message first and ask in one line. Other plugins' dialogs pass untouched.

plugins.name: question-forms
plugins.description: Every AI-DLC questions file becomes a form in one private artifact: the agent writes the questions as rows, you answer in the page, and the agent copies your answers word for word into the file's [Answer]: tags. Also renders text-only questions and board forms that sort cards into boxes.

plugins.name: story-points
plugins.description: For AI-DLC projects: keeps each intent's unit-points.csv (read by project-panel) with the developers' story-point estimates, typed with /story-points:set, picked in a review form with /story-points:review, or synced from Jira when the project's .story-points.json names a tracker; checks a Unit is estimated before it is claimed.

plugins.name: approval-gates
plugins.description: For AI-DLC projects: at every approval gate the stage's documents, the review brief and the completion summary become one page in the developer's private artifact, linked from the gate question, with a purpose-built view per document kind (entities, rules, components, units, stories, requirements, decisions, contracts, bolts, traceability) and ids linked across documents; a hook refuses the Approval question and the approved or rejected report until the page exists. Notes left in the page come back to the agent. Under the unit-end rhythm a Unit gets two pages instead: the plan page (every design stage, read once) and the unit-end page (what was built), built from a gate bundle whose JSON contract and validator ship with the plugin.

plugins.name: review-findings
plugins.description: Whenever review findings reach the developer (an AI-DLC stage review brief at a gate, or /code-review's findings), each open finding is shown in plain words with a suggested action, in chat and above one question: Fix, Accept (only when nothing is blocking) or Open in form, where each finding is sorted into fix, accept or reject with a reason. A hook enforces the order.

plugins.name: aidlc-session-titles
plugins.description: For AI-DLC projects: keeps every session that runs the workflow titled by what it is on — `<unit> — <stage>` on a Construction Unit, else `<phase> — <stage>` — read from the project's state (binding, claim, directive, stage graph), never from the agent. Set at each prompt and, in the desktop app, renamed mid-turn when the stage or Unit moves on.

plugins.name: unit-claim
plugins.description: For team AI-DLC Units: before a claim one dialog asks which design stages run and the approval rhythm (unit-end or per-stage), with a model's run-or-skip recommendation per stage drawn above it; typed answers are read by a model and refused when unclear. A hook refuses the claim until it is answered, claims with the chosen rhythm, and skips left-out stages for that Unit only.

plugins.name: aidlc-patches
plugins.description: For people who patch the AI-DLC engine in their own fork of awslabs/aidlc-workflows: investigate a bug to a failing test, check upstream first, keep the fork as an upstream release plus one commit per patch, release previews numbered from .101, pin projects to them, and send fixes upstream. Remembers your forks across plugin updates.

plugins.name: aidlc-ids
plugins.description: For AI-DLC projects: keeps the project's own id map (US, AC, FR, NFR, BR, Q, U, C, E, ADR, R and the rest), outside the project; /aidlc-ids:sync builds or refreshes it without a model turn, and the plugins' pages read it so every id they show is a link with a tooltip.
